clue.text: Will this make us up? I don't know

parts.note: write P where S stands, and the word us turns into up

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether something will cheer a group up, then shrugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer 1-2-1 to get an instruction: put P in place of S, which turns 'us' into 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: In a quiz, a contestant who has no idea of the response says 'pass' to move on.

clue.text: You've got to resort island and villa, finally free of San Salvador

indicators.note: to re-sort letters is to arrange them afresh, so the pooled letters are shuffled
free of signals that the letters of the next word are taken out of the pool before the shuffle
finally picks the last letter of villa

parts.note: taken as written, its three letters are removed

explanation.surface: A holiday tip: to unwind at an island villa you must get away from the city of San Salvador.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool ISLAND and A (last of villa), strike out S, A, N, and rearrange the remaining L, D, A, I. 'San Salvador' looks like the capital of El Salvador; only 'Salvador' is the definition, the painter's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish surrealist painter, so his first name stands for him.

clue.text: Bottom of the American barrel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American slang word for a person's bottom
second meaning: a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is also the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: In US English the word is slang for buttocks, and separately it names a large cask holding wine or ale.

clue.text: Perhaps unconnected wordplay etc solved here?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not linked to mains electricity or water, as a remote home may be
second meaning: a solver works out wordplay in the margin, away from the crossword's squares

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a joke at the solver's expense: the scribbling space beside the puzzle is literally beside the squares.
explanation.definitionFit: A house supplied by its own generator and well is said to live without links to the public utility networks.

clue.text: Artisan food preserves a name in style

indicators.note: preserves means holds safe within, so meal wraps round the rest

parts.note: a meal is food

indicators.note: in places the next pieces inside the word for style

parts.note: chic means stylishness

explanation.surface: A craft food producer bottles something in a fashionable way.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream the workmen who stage the play are the 'rude mechanicals', an old use meaning manual workers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's day the word was a noun for a manual labourer or craftsman.

clue.text: Starveling rejected jelly and cake

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the jelly word is turned round

parts.note: agar is a jelly made from seaweed
a muffin is a small cake

explanation.surface: A hungry waif turns down jelly and cake, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: Starveling is the tailor among the mechanicals in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A starveling is a thin, ill-fed person; a ragged, scruffy child fits that picture as a near synonym.

clue.text: Twist opening of canticle or its end once: not again

indicators.note: only the first two letters of the canticle word are twisted round, swapping places

parts.note: an anthem is a sacred song, like a canticle
its refers to the canticle, whose last letter is E

explanation.surface: A choirmaster's direction about the beginning of a hymn, and then a refusal to repeat it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first two letters of ANTHEM to get NATHEM, then add OR and the E ending ANTHEM. 'once' marks the answer as archaic: Spenser's word for 'never again'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb, literally 'never the more', meaning never again or no further.

clue.text: Broadcasting this way would be poor/average

indicators.note: broadcasting means sending out over the air, so it is the spoken sound that counts

parts.note: mean can mean both poor (shabby) and average

explanation.surface: Someone suggests that putting a programme out in this format would make it mediocre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is the answer itself: say it aloud and it sounds like a word meaning both poor and average.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's manner or bearing, the way they look and carry themselves.

clue.text: Napoleon's ailing limb's dressed with quince preparation

indicators.note: a limb dressed with the French word sits inside it, wrapped like a bandaged arm

parts.note: malade is French for ill, Napoleon being a Frenchman
an arm is a limb; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: The French emperor's sick arm is bandaged, with a poultice of quince.
explanation.walkthrough: Quince is the carpenter who directs the play in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The preserve's name comes from Portuguese marmelo, quince, from which it was first made before oranges.

clue.text: Snug Bar Tony's principal reasons not to get a round?

indicators.note: bar means except, so one letter is excluded

parts.words: reasons not to get a round
parts.note: being skint (British slang for penniless) and being tight (stingy) both stop someone buying drinks for the group

indicators.note: principal means first, so the opening letter of Tony's

explanation.surface: In a pub's cosy back room Tony's main excuses for not buying drinks are aired.
explanation.walkthrough: Join SKINT and TIGHT, then drop one T. A snug is a small private room in a British pub, and Snug is the joiner in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that fits tightly against the body is described as close-fitting, or cosily snug.

clue.text: Midway through June, Eva is born

indicators.note: the letters are taken from the middle of the run June Eva, straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A birth announcement: Eva arrives in the middle of June.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed before a maiden name, the French word indicates the family a woman was born into.

clue.text: Demon who delights I now see in Rugby

indicators.note: in puts the exclamation inside the rugby abbreviation

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union
ah is the exclamation of sudden understanding

explanation.surface: A spectator at a rugby match realises who the joyful star is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delights' is the twist: read it as de-lights, putting out the lights. In Hindu myth Rahu swallows the sun or moon, causing eclipses.
explanation.definitionFit: Rahu is the severed head of a Hindu demon who devours the sun and moon, extinguishing their light in eclipses.

clue.text: A sign of business that is open to question

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a busy place gives off a low steady drone, read business as busyness
second meaning: an interjection voicing doubt or hesitation

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'business' as busy-ness: a busy office or hive drones.
explanation.definitionFit: A low continuous drone signals activity, and the same sound uttered aloud expresses hesitant doubt.

clue.text: I despise fragmenting walls with dig, incidentally

indicators.note: walls means encloses, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
fragmenting means breaking into pieces, so the letters of I despise are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes crumbling masonry complains about walls while doing a bit of digging.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters SIDESIPE wrap round W.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideswipe is a passing critical remark made in the course of discussing something else.

clue.text: Cradle-songs or big band Jazz?

parts.note: to cradle a baby is to swing it gently
songs are music

explanation.surface: A question whether lullabies or big band jazz are meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cradle-songs' reads as lullabies, but split it: cradle gives one part, songs the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Swing was the style of jazz played by large dance orchestras of the 1930s and 1940s.

clue.text: The 24 5s here? Yes and no

parts.note: the rude mechanicals form a troupe within Shakespeare's Dream, but as actors they are hopeless rather than ideal

explanation.walkthrough: The 24 and 5 entries make RUDE MECHANICALS, the amateur actors in A Midsummer Night's Dream. They are a team in the Dream, so yes; but a perfect line-up they are not.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an ideal group of players, while literally reading as the company within the play.

clue.text: A belt — all there is to keep miner's leader on pithead

indicators.note: to keep means to hold, so the sane word holds the following pieces

parts.note: someone all there is sane

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the miner's initial comes first
leader picks the first letter of miner's

parts.note: in mining the brow is the top of a pit shaft

explanation.surface: Apparently a belt holds everything needed to keep the mine foreman at the shaft head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sam Browne is a military belt with a supporting strap over the right shoulder, named after a general.

clue.text: How enjoyable to squeeze new spots

indicators.note: to squeeze means to hold tightly, so the exclamation grips the next letter

parts.note: ace! is an exclamation of delight

explanation.surface: Someone finds squeezing fresh pimples satisfying.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'squeeze' about pimples, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, so the word stands for a rash of them.

clue.text: Monitor of suspect pulse around middle of summer afternoon

parts.note: a PI, private investigator, keeps watch on a suspect

indicators.note: around means the pulse word goes round the next letters

parts.note: a pea is a pulse, an edible seed

indicators.note: middle of picks the central pair of letters in summer

explanation.surface: Something tracks a dubious heartbeat around midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: PEA opens to take MM, the middle of summer. PIP EMMA is old military phonetic slang for the letters PM.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the old signallers' pronunciation of PM, the abbreviation for post meridiem, the hours after noon.

clue.text: Overly protective of "Bravo Bill", copper's top snout

indicators.note: protective of means shielding, so the first word wraps round the rest

parts.note: too means overly
B is Bravo in the NATO alphabet
AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: top picks the first letter of copper's

explanation.surface: A police officer's main informant is too protective of someone called Bravo Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snout' looks like the police informer the surface suggests; it is prison slang for tobacco, and Snout is the tinker in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: In British prison slang snout is a word for cigarettes or rolling leaf for smoking.

clue.text: Venetian madam cut short during it?

indicators.note: during means within, so the shortened word sits inside the sex appeal letters

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is crosswordese for it

indicators.note: short means the last letter is lost

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore them

explanation.surface: A Venetian lady is snubbed in the middle of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title for a married woman, equivalent to Mrs or madam, used in Venice as elsewhere in Italy.

clue.text: Back in the past the origin of messages

definitions.text: Back in the past the origin of messages

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so the past word reads in reverse

parts.note: ago means in the past

indicators.note: the origin is the start, so the first letter of messages

explanation.surface: A historian's remark that long ago lay the source of written communication.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogam, or Ogham, is the ancient Irish alphabet of strokes carved on stones, an early form of writing.

clue.text: I'm told Raymond's the man who's going to make trouble

indicators.note: I'm told means heard by report, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.words: Raymond's the man who's going to
parts.note: Ray's for Raymond's and he'll for the man who's going to, said together

explanation.surface: Gossip that Raymond is the fellow about to cause a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to create a loud disturbance or protest angrily.

clue.text: Permitted to escape deadly sentient computer

indicators.note: to escape means getting out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: lethal means deadly
let means permitted

explanation.surface: A dangerous computer is allowed to break free.
explanation.definitionFit: HAL 9000 is the self-aware machine in Kubrick's film 2001: A Space Odyssey.

clue.text: Twins, very audibly!

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: too means very

explanation.surface: A loud exclamation about a pair of twins.
explanation.definitionFit: Twins come as a pair, a number one more than one.

clue.text: Was sorry for wiggling rear, showing more than a little cheek

definitions.text: showing more than a little cheek

indicators.note: wiggling the rear means only the final pair of letters is switched round

parts.note: rued means regretted

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for shaking their bottom, which displayed quite a lot of buttock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheek' reads as a buttock in the surface; in the definition it is impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude behaviour is impolite, a good deal more than mere impudence or cheekiness.

clue.text: Like maiden pursuing favourable outcome of playing flute?

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the like and maiden words come after

parts.note: a win is the best result of a game
EG, for example, means like
a lass is a maiden

explanation.surface: A girl chasing victory in a flute recital.
explanation.walkthrough: A flute is a tall narrow glass for champagne, hence the question mark; Flute is also the bellows-mender in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A champagne flute is one type of stemmed drinking glass, so it is an example.

clue.text: Gay son, Joshua, finally wriggling free of San Francisco?

indicators.note: wriggling means twisting about, so the pooled letters are rearranged
free of signals that the letters of the next word are taken out of the pool first
finally picks the last letter of Joshua

parts.note: taken as written, its three letters are removed

explanation.surface: A gay son named Joshua squirms out of San Francisco.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool GAY, SON and A, strike out S, A, N, and rearrange the remaining G, Y, O, A. 'San Francisco' looks like the city; the question mark flags Francisco as the painter's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the Spanish painter, so his first name stands for him, as an example.

clue.text: Lead characters of thematic play, somewhere within

indicators.note: lead characters are the leading letters, so only the title's opening run is kept

parts.note: the play behind the puzzle's theme is A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: The leading roles of a play with a theme, somewhere in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead characters' looks like the star roles; it means the first letters of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of, surrounded by.

clue.text: I've seen the game with second half's dismissal of Ramsey, nil-nil written all over it

indicators.note: the two noughts are scattered across the letters, one after each
dismissal means sending away, so Ramsey's first name leaves the word

parts.note: the word half, from which letters are taken
Alf Ramsey managed England's 1966 World Cup winners
O, a zero, is nil
the second O of the goalless score

explanation.surface: A football fan watched a match in which Ramsey's side failed in the second half, a goalless draw being the obvious outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: HALF without ALF leaves H; S and H are then each followed by an O from nil-nil.
explanation.definitionFit: So-ho was the huntsman's cry on sighting a hare, announcing that the quarry had been spotted.

clue.text: Concern with conviction

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a business, as in a going concern

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single phrase, worry over a court verdict; split it after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is called a firm, and a belief held resolutely is called firm, two separate senses.

clue.text: Awful lethargy takes over in premature retirement

indicators.note: takes means takes in, so the reworked letters surround the next piece
awful means dreadful, signalling that lethargy's letters are reworked
over means turned over, so the word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: Terrible sluggishness sets in and someone stops work too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged EARLYGHT takes in NI, which is 'in' read backwards. 'retirement' suggests leaving work; here it is retiring to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to bed sooner than usual is a common idiom, retiring for the evening ahead of the normal hour.
